**Relevant as prior art / category peer — not as something orso depends on.**

[cloudflare/vibesdk](https://github.com/cloudflare/vibesdk) (~5.5k★, [build.cloudflare.dev](https://build.cloudflare.dev)) is Cloudflare’s open-source “build your own vibe-coding platform.” Same *loop* as orso’s design pitch (prompt → agent edits → live preview → restore points), very different architecture and product bet.

| | **orso** | **VibeSDK** |
|---|---|---|
| Where it runs | Local Rust daemon | Cloudflare Workers / Durable Objects |
| Agent | Your CLIs (Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Cursor) | Cloudflare Think + AI Gateway |
| Project shape | Real Astro repo + content collections | Generated full-stack apps in SpaceDO |
| Preview | Local Astro `dev` + HMR proxy | Bundle → Dynamic Worker |
| History | Git + GitHub PRs | Cloudflare Artifacts |
| Publish | Merge to `main` / Pages-style deploy | Deploy preview / export |

orso’s own spec even calls out the same UX target: a **local Lovable-style** builder (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-orso-lovable-builder-design.md`). VibeSDK is closer to **hosted Lovable infrastructure** (and Cloudflare has said Lovable itself runs on Dynamic Workers at huge scale).

**So for this repo:**
- **Useful to study** if you ever want a *hosted / multi-tenant* orso (isolation, Dynamic Worker previews, Artifacts, agent-in-DO patterns).
- **Not a drop-in** for current orso — you’re local-first, Astro/CMS/GitHub-native, and you already treat Cloudflare mainly as a **site deploy target**, not as the builder runtime.
- **Competitive framing**: same category (“vibe site/app builder”), opposite thesis (local + your agent subs vs cloud + CF stack).

content.text:
**VibeSDK owns the agent loop; orso wraps external coding CLIs.** That’s the core difference.

### What each agent *is*

| | **orso** | **VibeSDK (Think)** |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | Spawns Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Cursor as subprocesses | In-process `@cloudflare/think` Durable Object |
| Protocol | ACP over stdio (`session/prompt`, tool events, permissions) | Model ↔ tools loop inside Think (AI SDK / AI Gateway) |
| Auth / billing | User’s own CLI login / subscription | Platform API keys via AI Gateway (+ rate limits / credits) |
| Install | Pinned managed runtimes in `agent-runtime.lock.json` | Deployed Worker code; models chosen in `AGENT_CONFIG` |

orso: pick a provider → resolve managed binary → launch ACP argv (`cursor-agent acp`, `opencode acp`, or `@agentclientprotocol/*-acp` bridges).  
VibeSDK: one `ThinkAgent` per app, configured with `configureVibe({ model, systemPrompt, previewUrl })`.

### How they’re steered

**orso — inject guide into *their* CLIs**
- Shared `agent_guide()` = orso vocabulary + git “change” rules
- Claude: `--append-system-prompt`
- Codex: `developer_instructions=…`
- OpenCode: per-project `opencode.json` `instructions`
- Cursor: git-excluded `.cursor/rules/orso-changes.mdc`
- Model: whatever that CLI lists (`claude` aliases, `codex` cache, `opencode`/`cursor` `models`)
- Permissions: UI answers ACP `request_permission`, or `auto_approve` → each CLI’s bypass flag (`--force`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, etc.)
- Tools: **whatever the CLI has** (bash, edit, etc.) — orso does not define a tool set

**VibeSDK — first-party agent with a closed tool surface**
- System prompt: model-family templates (`gemini.txt`, `anthropic.txt`, …) + project context
- Skills: shipped `SKILL.md`s (file structure, AI bindings, frontend design variants)
- Explicit tools only: `read/write/edit/list/find/grep/delete`, `commit`, `deploy_space`, `ask_questions`, `get_browser_console_logs`, `set_title`
- **`workspaceBash = false`** — no shell
- Default Think model: `google-ai-studio/gemini-3.6-flash`; multi-role `AGENT_CONFIG` for older phasic/agentic modes (blueprint, debugger, etc.)
- Caps: `maxSteps = 25`, credit metering per turn

### Practical takeaway

- **orso** configures *which vendor agent to run* and *what product rules to inject*; capability and sandboxing come from Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor.
- **VibeSDK** configures *the agent itself*: model routing, prompts, skills, and a curated non-bash tool belt aimed at Cloudflare full-stack apps + Dynamic Worker deploy.

Closest overlap: both stream chat + tool activity and commit/restore. Closest gap: orso is “bring your own coding agent”; VibeSDK is “bring your own model keys to *our* agent.”

Using brainstorming — this looks **architectural**, so I’ll sketch options here and stop for your call before any spec/plan.

**Understanding:** you want orso’s assistant closer to VibeSDK: a **fixed, product-owned tool belt** (no free-form bash), plus **loadable skills**, instead of “whatever Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor already can do.” Assumption: the goal is safer/more predictable edits for non-technical users, not just mirroring Cloudflare.

### Hard constraint

Today orso **does not own the tool surface**. It owns launch, ACP streaming, permissions UI, and a system guide. Tools live inside each vendor CLI. You can’t get a *true* closed surface while those CLIs remain the agent — only soft gates.

You already have skill-shaped content (`skills/working-in-orso`, plus `agent_guide()`), but that’s **prompt/rules injection**, not Think-style skill loading with a closed toolkit.

### Three realistic paths

**1. Soft close (keep BYO agents)**  
Deny/allow via ACP `request_permission` + per-provider flags (e.g. no bash / no network). Ship skills as project files each CLI already reads (`.cursor/rules`, Claude skills, OpenCode instructions, `AGENTS.md`).  
- Pros: stays on your current architecture  
- Cons: not enforceable; each vendor differs; bash can still sneak through when `auto_approve` is on  

**2. Hybrid: orso as ACP *client* to *one* owned agent**  
Ship a single orso agent (or thin wrapper) that speaks ACP but only exposes `read/write/edit/grep/…`, `orso ctl`, commit, maybe deploy-status — **no bash**. Skills = `SKILL.md` catalog orso injects. Vendor CLIs become optional “power mode.”  
- Pros: real closed surface; skills become a real product feature; still ACP/UI  
- Cons: you now maintain an agent loop, models, and quality — the VibeSDK cost center  

**3. Full Think-like rewrite**  
Replace BYO CLIs with a hosted/in-process agent (models via gateway, DO workspace, etc.).  
- Pros: strongest control  
- Cons: abandons orso’s core bet (local + your subscriptions)

### Skills specifically

Skills are the easy half **if** you own the loop (path 2/3): catalog in system prompt + `load_skill` tool, like VibeSDK.  
With path 1, “skills” stay **files the foreign agent may or may not honor**.

Using brainstorming — this stays **architectural**. You’re asking for **both**, so the design is: keep vendor CLIs as the engine, add a **real policy layer** around them (orso already does this for git checkout).

**Understanding:** you still want Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor as the agents, but fewer foot-guns for non-technical users — not a VibeSDK-style owned agent. Assumption: “secured toolbelt” means **hard blocks + default-deny**, not just nicer prompts.

### What you already have
- Soft: `agent_guide()` / `skills/working-in-orso` (ask, don’t enforce)
- Hard: `git` shim blocks HEAD-moving `checkout`/`switch`
- Soft/hard mix: ACP permission prompts, but **`auto_approve` currently means “bypass the CLI’s sandbox”** (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--force`, Opencode `permission: allow`) — that fights a secured toolbelt

### Design that gives you both

Keep BYO CLIs. Add a **policy plane** in three layers:

**1. Command shims (hard, like git)**  
Extend the PATH-shim idea beyond checkout:
- Block: `reset --hard`, `rebase`, force-push, `push` to `main`, `worktree add`, maybe `clean -fd`
- Optionally wrap `rm` / `mv` outside the project, or package managers that escape the site  
Same seam as today’s git shim: agent still “has git,” but dangerous forms die with a clear error.

**2. ACP permission policy (default-deny classes)**  
Instead of allow-all / ask-everything:
- **Auto-allow:** read, edit in-project, `orso ctl *`, normal `git add/commit/status/diff`
- **Ask once / ask always:** `npm install`, network, new deps
- **Hard deny:** shell that looks destructive, path escape, publish/share equivalents  
`auto_approve` should mean “auto-allow the *safe* class,” not “turn off the CLI’s guardrails.” That’s the important product flip.

**3. Skills as the preferred path (not the only control)**  
Promote current guides into a small skill pack the CLIs load (`working-in-orso`, content edits, preview repair via `orso ctl`). Skills steer; shims + policy enforce.

```text
UI chat → ACP → vendor CLI (tools stay theirs)
                ↑
         orso policy: shim PATH + ACP allow/deny + skills
```

### What this is *not*
You still won’t get VibeSDK’s exact closed surface (`workspaceBash = false`). Vendor CLIs keep bash/edit tools. You get a **product-defined envelope**: “CLI power, orso-shaped blast radius.”

---

**One question:** when you say “less things can go wrong,” which failure mode matters most first?

1. **Destructive git** (reset/rebase/wrong branch/push)  
2. **Filesystem** (delete/move the wrong stuff)  
3. **Shell/deps** (`npm` / curl / random scripts)  
4. **Product actions** (publish / share / greenlight by mistake)

Today the daemon puts an orso `git` **shim first on the agent’s `PATH`**. That shim:

- **Blocks:** HEAD-moving `checkout` / `switch` (branch changes, `-b`/`-B`, detach, etc.)
- **Allows:** everything else (`status`, `diff`, `add`, `commit`, `fetch`, `merge`, path restores like `checkout -- file`, …)

### What “limit a set of git tools” looks like here

Same seam — extend the shim from “block checkout” to an **allowlist or denylist**, e.g.:

| Allow (typical) | Deny (typical) |
|---|---|
| `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show` | `checkout`/`switch` (already) |
| `add`, `commit` | `reset --hard`, `rebase`, `clean -fd` |
| `fetch`, `merge` (maybe) | `push` (esp. to `main`), `worktree` |

- Hard only if the agent calls `git` via `PATH`. Absolute `/usr/bin/git` or a vendor-bundled git can bypass unless you sandbox further.
- Prompt/skills alone won’t enforce; the shim (or OS sandbox) does.

### Always allow (read / inspect)

| Command | Why |
|---|---|
| `status` | See dirty tree |
| `diff` | See changes (incl. `--staged`) |
| `log` | History on current change |
| `show` | Inspect a commit/file at a rev |
| `ls-files` | Tracked paths |
| `rev-parse` | Resolve SHAs / current branch |
| `branch` *(list only: no `-d/-D/-m/-c`, no create)* | See branch name |
| `describe` | Optional; harmless |
| `blame` | Optional; read-only |
| `remote -v` / `remote` *(list only)* | See remotes; no add/remove |

### Allow (work on the current change)

| Command | Why |
|---|---|
| `add` | Stage for commit |
| `commit` | Save work (plus orso’s turn-end checkpoint) |
| `rm` | Remove tracked files cleanly |
| `mv` | Rename tracked files |
| `restore` / `checkout -- <paths>` / `checkout <tree-ish> -- <paths>` | Discard or restore **paths only** (HEAD stays put) |

| `merge` *(no `--abort` needed as separate? allow `--abort`)* | Sync `origin/main` into the current change |
| `merge --abort` | Recover a bad sync |

### Explicitly deny (everything else), including

- `checkout` / `switch` that move HEAD *(already)*
- `push`, `pull` *(pull = fetch+merge with fewer controls; prefer fetch+merge)*
- `rebase`, `reset`, `clean`, `stash` *(hard mode)*
- `worktree`, `submodule`
- `branch -b/-D/-d/-m`, `tag` mutate
- `remote add/remove/set-url`

- **Block** `-c` / `--exec-path` tricks that redefine aliases to escape the list (or strip `-c` entirely for agents).
- Only the app may set `ORSO_ALLOW_CHECKOUT=1` for real branch switches.

### What the agent can still do for the user

Inspect the repo → edit files (CLI file tools) → `add`/`commit` → `fetch` + `merge origin/main` → restore individual files if a change goes wrong. Publishing, sharing, switching changes stay app-only.

# Secured agent toolbelt (design)

Date: 2026-11-25  
Status: Approved (brainstorming)  
Tracker: GitHub Issues, Blaise1030/cms

## Summary

Keep vendor coding CLIs (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor) as the agent engine. Add an orso **policy plane** so fewer destructive operations succeed for non-technical users. Skills on disk steer; shims and ACP policy enforce.

## Goals

1. Agents can still inspect and edit the current change and sync with `main`.
2. Destructive or product-owned git/product actions are hard-blocked or require explicit approval.
3. `auto_approve` means “auto-allow the safe class”, not “disable the CLI sandbox”.

## Non-goals (v1)

- Replacing CLIs with an owned Think-style agent.
- OS-level sandbox / blocking absolute `/usr/bin/git`.
- Closed tool surface identical to VibeSDK (`workspaceBash = false`).

## Architecture

```
UI chat → ACP → vendor CLI
                ↑
         orso policy: PATH git shim + ACP allow/ask/deny + skills files
```

### Layer 1 — Git shim allowlist (slice 1)

Extend `src/git_shim.rs` from “block HEAD-moving checkout/switch” to **default-deny** except an allowlist.

**Allow**

| Command | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `ls-files`, `rev-parse`, `blame`, `describe` | Read / inspect |
| `branch` | List only (no `-d/-D/-m/-c/-C`, no create) |
| `remote`, `remote -v` | List only (no add/remove/set-url) |
| `add`, `commit`, `rm`, `mv` | Work on current change |
| `restore` | Working tree / index restore |
| `checkout` / path forms | Only path restores (`checkout -- <paths>`, `checkout <tree-ish> -- <paths>`); bare `checkout` with no args may pass as no-op |
| `fetch` | |
| `merge`, `merge --abort` | Sync with main; recover |

**Deny (examples):** HEAD-moving `checkout`/`switch` (unless `ORSO_ALLOW_CHECKOUT=1` for the app), `push`, `pull`, `rebase`, `reset`, `clean`, `stash`, `worktree`, mutating `branch`/`tag`/`remote`/`config`, unknown subcommands.

**Escape:** `-c` / `--exec-path` that could redefine aliases: strip or deny `-c` for agents (prefer deny any `-c` / `--exec-path` in the shim argv).

**Messages:** Distinct stderr, e.g. `orso: git <cmd> is not allowed from the assistant` vs the existing draft-switch message.

**App:** `ORSO_ALLOW_CHECKOUT=1` still permits the app’s HEAD-moving checkout/switch only.

### Layer 2 — ACP permission policy + safer `auto_approve` (slice 2)

Classify ACP `session/request_permission` (and tool metadata when present):

- **Auto-allow:** in-project reads/edits, `orso ctl *`, allowlisted git.
- **Ask:** network, package install, ambiguous shell.
- **Deny:** destructive shell, path escape, publish/share equivalents.

`auto_approve` auto-allows the safe class only; stop appending `--dangerously-skip-permissions` / `--force` / Opencode `permission: allow` as the default meaning of that toggle.

### Layer 3 — Skills (done / soft)

VibeSDK frontend-design skills vendored under `{orso.json root}/.agents/skills/` on init. Soft guidance only.

## Phasing

1. **Slice 1:** Git allowlist in `git_shim.rs` + unit tests.
2. **Slice 2:** ACP policy + `auto_approve` semantics.
3. Later: optional OS sandbox; document residual bypass (absolute git path).

## Success criteria

- Agent `git push` / `git reset --hard` / `git checkout other-branch` fail via the shim with a clear message.
- Agent `git status` / `git add` / `git commit` / `git fetch` / `git merge origin/main` / path `checkout -- file` still work.
- App draft switching still works with `ORSO_ALLOW_CHECKOUT=1`.
- Existing project skills unrelated to git are unchanged.
